body.text: Madhyamaka - śālistambasūtram |
body.translated_text: <s>Madhyamaka</s>-<s>Śālistambasūtra</s> (The Rice Stalk Sūtra from the Madhyamaka Perspective).

body.text: namo buddhāya ||
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.translated_text: Neither ceasing nor arising, neither annihilated nor eternal,
neither one in meaning nor many in meaning, neither coming nor going —
He who taught <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the auspicious pacification of conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañcopaśama</s>),
the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> — I salute Him, the foremost of teachers.

body.text: pratītyasamutpāda iti kasmāducyate? sahetukaḥ sapratyayo nāhetuko nāpratyaya ityucyate | atha ca punarayaṃ pratītyasamutpādo dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate | katamābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate? hetūpanibandhataḥ pratyayopanibandhataśceti | so 'pi dvividho draṣṭavyaḥ - bāhyaśca ādhyātmikaśca ||
body.translated_text: Why is it called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)? Because it has causes and conditions, and is not without cause or without conditions — thus it is called [so]. And furthermore, this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> arises from two kinds of causes. From which two kinds of causes does it arise? From the foundation of causes (<s>hetūpanibandha</s>) and from the foundation of conditions (<s>pratyayopanibandha</s>). And this should be understood as twofold: external and internal.

body.text: tatra bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandhaḥ katamaḥ? yadidaṃ bījādaṅkuraḥ, aṅkurātpatram, patrātkāṇḍam, kāṇḍānnāḍam, nāḍāddaṇḍaḥ, daṇḍādgarbhaḥ, garbhācchūkaḥ, śūkātpuṣpam, puṣpātphalamiti | asati bīje aṅkuro na bhavati, evaṃ yāvat asati puṣpe phalaṃ na bhavati | sati tu bīje aṅkurasya abhinirvṛttirbhavati, evaṃ yāvat sati ca puṣpe phalasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | tatra ca punarbījasya naivaṃ bhavati - ahamaṅkuraṃ nirvartayāmīti | etena nirīhatvam | aṅkurasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bījenābhinirvartita iti | evaṃ yāvatpuṣpasya naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ phalamabhinirvartayāmīti | phalasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ puṣpeṇābhinirvartita iti | atha bīje sati ca kāraṇabhūte aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttiḥ prādurbhāvo bhavati, evaṃ yāvatpuṣpe sati phalasyābhinirvṛttiḥ prādurbhāvo bhavati | evaṃ ca bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the foundation of causes of external dependent origination? It is this: from a seed arises a sprout, from a sprout a leaf, from a leaf a stalk, from a stalk a stem, from a stem a bud, from a bud a sheath, from a sheath a flower, and from a flower a fruit. If there is no seed, the sprout does not come into being; likewise, if there is no flower, the fruit does not come into being. But when there is a seed, the production of the sprout occurs; likewise, when there is a flower, the production of the fruit occurs. And therein, the seed does not think: 'I produce a sprout' — by this, its effortlessness [is shown]. The sprout also does not think: 'I am produced by the seed.' Likewise, the flower does not think: 'I produce a fruit.' The fruit also does not think: 'I am produced by the flower.' But when the seed is present as a cause, the production and manifestation of the sprout occurs; likewise, when the flower is present, the production and manifestation of the fruit occurs. Thus should the foundation of causes of external dependent origination be understood.

children.translated_text: [Reference: MŚālSū, Vaidya 109]

children.text: ) punaḥ kathaṃ bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ? ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt | svabhāvadhāraṇāddhātuḥ | katameṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt? yadidaṃ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśadhātusamanvayādbāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | tatra pṛthividhāturbījasya saṃdhāraṇakṛtyaṃ karoti, abdhāturbījaṃ snehayati, tejodhāturbījaṃ paripācayati, vāyudhāturbījamabhinirharati, ākāśadhāturbījasyānāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karoti, ṛturapi bījasya pariṇāmakṛtyaṃ karoti | asatsu pratyayeṣu bījādaṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirna bhavati | yadā bāhyaśca pṛthivīdhāturavikalo bhavati, evamaptejovāyvākāśaṛtudhātavaścāvikalā bhavanti, tatasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ samavāyādbīje nirudhyamāne aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | tatra pṛthivīdhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bījasya dhāraṇākṛtyaṃ karomi iti | evaṃ yāvadṛtorapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bījasya pariṇāmanākṛtyaṃ karomi iti | aṅkurasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanita iti | atha punaḥ satsu pratyayeṣu teṣu bīje nirudhyamāne aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | sa cāyamaṅkuro na svayaṃkṛto na parakṛto nobhayakṛto neśvaranirmito na kālapariṇāmito na prakṛtisaṃbhūto nākāraṇādhīno nāpyahetusamutpannaśca | pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśadhātusamavāyādbije nirudhyamāne aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | evaṃ bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) Furthermore, how should the foundation of conditions of external dependent origination be understood? Through the combination of six elements (<s>dhātus</s>). An element (<s>dhātu</s>) is so called because it maintains its own nature. Through the combination of which six elements? The foundation of conditions of external dependent origination should be understood through the combination of the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and season. Therein, the earth element performs the function of supporting the seed; the water element moistens the seed; the fire element ripens the seed; the wind element draws out the seed; the space element performs the function of non-obstruction for the seed; and the season also performs the function of transforming the seed. In the absence of conditions, the production of a sprout from a seed does not occur. When the external earth element is complete, and likewise the water, fire, wind, space, and season elements are complete, then through the combination of all of them, as the seed ceases, the production of the sprout occurs. Therein, the earth element does not think: 'I perform the function of supporting the seed.' Likewise, even the season does not think: 'I perform the function of transforming the seed.' The sprout also does not think: 'I am produced by these conditions.' But when the conditions are present, as the seed ceases, the production of the sprout occurs. And this sprout is not self-made, not made by another, not made by both, not created by a god (<s>Īśvara</s>), not transformed by time, not arisen from primordial nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>), not dependent on a single cause, and yet not arisen without a cause. Through the combination of the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, and space, as the seed ceases, the production of the sprout occurs. Thus should the foundation of conditions of external dependent origination be understood.

body.text: tatra bāhyaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairdraṣṭavyaḥ | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? na śāśvatato nocchedato na saṃkrāntitaḥ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ tatsadṛśānuprabandhataśceti | kathaṃ na śāśvatata iti? yasmādanyo 'ṅkuro 'nyadbījam, na ca yadeva bījaṃ sa evāṅkuraḥ | atha ca punarbījaṃ nirudhyate, aṅkuraścotpadyate | ato na śāśvatataḥ || kathaṃ punarnocchedataḥ? na ca pūrvaniruddhādbījādaṅkuro niṣpadyate, nāpyaniruddhādbījāt | api ca bījaṃ ca nirudhyate, tasminneva samaye 'ṅkura utpadyate, tulādaṇḍonnāmāvanāmavat | ato nocchedataḥ || kathaṃ na saṃkrāntitaḥ? visadṛśo bījādaṅkura ityato na saṃkrāntitaḥ || kathaṃ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ? parīttaṃ bījamupyate(vyāptitvāt - avyā) vipulaṃ phalamabhinirvartayati, ityataḥ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ || kathaṃ tatsadṛśānubandhataḥ? yādṛśaṃ bījamupyate tādṛśaṃ phalamabhinirvartayati, ityataḥ tatsadṛśānubandhataśceti | evaṃ bāhyaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairdraṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the external dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) should be viewed through five reasons. Which five? Not from the standpoint of eternalism, not from the standpoint of annihilationism, not from the standpoint of transmigration, from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause, and from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the [cause]. How is it not from the standpoint of eternalism? Because the sprout is one thing and the seed is another — the seed itself is not the sprout. Moreover, the seed ceases and the sprout arises. Therefore, it is not from the standpoint of eternalism. How is it not from the standpoint of annihilationism? The sprout does not arise from a seed that has previously ceased, nor from one that has not ceased. Rather, the seed ceases, and at that very moment the sprout arises — like the rising and falling of the beam of a balance. Therefore, it is not from the standpoint of annihilationism. How is it not from the standpoint of transmigration? Because the sprout is dissimilar from the seed — therefore, it is not from the standpoint of transmigration. How is it from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause? A small seed is sown, yet it produces a vast fruit — therefore, it is from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause. How is it from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the [cause]? Whatever kind of seed is sown, that same kind of fruit it produces — therefore, it is from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the cause. Thus should the external dependent origination be viewed through five reasons.

children.translated_text: [MŚālSū, Vaidya 110]

children.text: ) tatra punaścādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandhaḥ katamaḥ? yadidamavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, yāvajjātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamiti | avidyā cennābhaviṣyat, naivaṃ saṃskārāḥ prajñāsyante | evaṃ yāvadyadi jātirnābhaviṣyat(skandhānāṃ pañcānāṃ prādurbhāvo jātiriti), tatra jarāmaraṇaṃ na prajñāsyate | atha ca satyāmavidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇāmabhinirvṛttirbhavatīti | tatrāvidyāyā naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ saṃskārānabhinirvartayāmīti | punaḥ sarvasaṃskārāṇāmapyevaṃ na bhavati - vayamavidyayā abhinirvartitā iti | evaṃ yāvajjāteḥ(skandhaprādurbhāvasya) naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ jarāmaraṇamabhinirvartayāmīti | jarāmaraṇasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ jātyābhinirvartita iti | atha ca satyāmavidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇāmabhinirvṛttiebhavati prādurbhāva eva, evaṃ yāvat jātyāṃ satyāṃ jarāmaraṇasyābhinirvṛttiḥ prādurbhāvo bhavati | evamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) Now, what is the dependence on conditions of the internal dependent origination? It is this: formations conditioned by ignorance, up to aging-and-death conditioned by birth. If ignorance had not existed, formations would not be perceived. Likewise, up to: if birth (the manifestation of the five aggregates) had not existed, aging-and-death would not be perceived there. But when ignorance is present, the production of formations occurs. Therein, ignorance does not think: 'I produce formations.' Nor do all formations think: 'We are produced by ignorance.' Likewise, up to: birth (the manifestation of aggregates) does not think: 'I produce aging-and-death.' Nor does aging-and-death think: 'I am produced by birth.' But when ignorance is present, the production — the very manifestation — of formations occurs. Likewise, up to: when birth is present, the production — the very manifestation — of aging-and-death occurs. Thus should the dependence on conditions of the internal dependent origination be understood.

body.text: punaḥ kathamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ? yadidaṃ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśavijñānadhātūnāṃ samavāyādādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | tatrādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pṛthivīdhātuḥ katama iti? yo 'yaṃ kāyasya saṃśleṣataḥ(saṃparkāt) kaṭhinabhāvamabhinirvartayati, ayamucyate pṛthivīdhātuḥ || yaḥ punaḥ kāyasya parigrahakṛtvaṃ(svīkārasaṃcayakṛtyaṃ) karoti, ayamucyate abdhātuḥ || yaśca punaḥ kāyasya aśitaṃ pītaṃ bhakṣitaṃ paripācayati ayamucyate tejodhātuḥ || yaḥ kāyasya āśvāsapraśvāsakṛtyaṃ(vāyorākarṣaṇamāśvāsaḥ etatkṛtyaṃ)karoti, ayamucyate vāyudhātuḥ || yaḥ kāyasyāntaḥśauṣiryabhāvamabhinirvartayati, ayamucyate ākāśadhātuḥ || yo nāmarūpamabhinirvartayati naḍakalāpayogena cakṣurādipañcavidhavijñānakāya(vijñānasamūha) - saṃyuktaṃ sāsravaṃ(sāvaraṇaṃ) manovijñānam, ayamucyate vijñānadhātuḥ || asatsu pratyayeṣu kāyasyotpattirna bhavati | yadā cādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivīdhāturavikalo bhavati, evamaptejovāyvākāśavijñānadhātavaścāvikalā bhavanti, tatsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ samavāyātkāyasyotpattirbhavati | tatra pṛthivīdhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasya kaṭhinatvamabhinirvartayāmīti | (

children.translated_text: [MŚālSū, Vaidya 111]

children.text: ) abdhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasyānuparigrahaṃ karomīti | tejodhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasya aśitapītakhāditaṃ paripācayāmīti | vāyudhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasyāśvāsapraśvāsakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ākāśadhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasyāntaḥśauṣiryabhāvamabhinirvartayāmīti | vijñānadhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyamabhinirvartayāmīti | kāyasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayaviśeṣairjanita iti || atha ca satsu pratyayeṣu kāyasyotpattirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: The water element does not think: 'I perform the function of holding together the body.' The fire element does not think: 'I digest what is eaten, drunk, and consumed by the body.' The wind element does not think: 'I perform the function of inhalation and exhalation for the body.' The space element does not think: 'I produce the state of internal hollowness of the body.' The consciousness element does not think: 'I produce the body.' And the body also does not think: 'I am produced by these particular conditions.' Yet when the conditions are present, the arising of the body occurs.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, how should the foundation of conditions (<s>pratyayopanibandha</s>) of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) be understood? It is this: the foundation of conditions of internal dependent origination should be understood through the combination of the elements (<s>dhātus</s>) of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness. Therein, what is the earth element of internal dependent origination? That which produces the state of hardness from the cohesion of the body — this is called the earth element. That which performs the function of holding together (appropriating and accumulating) the body — this is called the water element. That which digests what is eaten, drunk, and consumed by the body — this is called the fire element. That which performs the function of inhalation and exhalation (the drawing in of air is inhalation — this function) of the body — this is called the wind element. That which produces the state of internal hollowness of the body — this is called the space element. That which produces <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) — the mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) that is tainted (<s>sāsrava</s>, with obstructions), conjoined with the five types of consciousness-bodies (<s>vijñānakāya</s>) beginning with the eye, like a bundle of reeds — this is called the consciousness element. When conditions are absent, the arising of the body does not occur. When the internal earth element is complete, and likewise the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are complete, then through the combination of all of them, the arising of the body occurs. Therein, the earth element does not think: 'I produce the hardness of the body.'

body.text: tatra pṛthivīdhāturnātmā (na mukto na baddho) na jīvo na janturna manujo na mānavo na strī na puruṣo na napuṃsakaṃ na cāhaṃ na ca mama, nāpyanyasya kasyacit |(evaṃ abdhātustejodhāturvāyudhāturākāśadhāturvijñānadhāturnātmā.............. nāpyanyasya kasyacit) ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the earth element is not a self (<s>ātman</s>), not a living being (<s>jīva</s>), not a creature (<s>jantu</s>), not a human (<s>manuja</s>), not a man (<s>mānava</s>), not a woman, not a man, not neuter, not 'I,' and not 'mine,' and not anyone else's. (Similarly, the water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element are not a self... and not anyone else's.)

body.text: tatrāvidyā katamā? yā eṣveva ṣaḍdhātuṣu ekasaṃjñā piṇḍasaṃjñā nityasaṃjñā dhruvasaṃjñā śāśvatasaṃjñā sukhasaṃjñā sattvajīvajantupoṣapuruṣapudgalamanujamānavasaṃjñā ahaṃkāramamakārasaṃjñā, evamādi vividhamajñānam, iyamucyate avidyeti | evamavidyāyāṃ satyāṃ viṣayeṣu rāgadveṣamohāḥ pravartante | tatra ye rāgadveṣamohā viṣayeṣu, amī ucyante saṃskārā iti || vastuprajñaptiḥ(indriyavijñānacetanā) vijñānam || vijñānasahajāścatvāra upādānaskandhāḥ, tannāmarūpam | nāmarūpasaṃśritānīndriyāṇi ṣaḍāyatanam | trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśaḥ, (viṣayendriyavijñānasaṃnipāta ityarthaḥ) | sparśānubhāvo vedanā | vedanādhyavasānaṃ tṛṣṇā(adhyavasānaṃ kāṅkṣā sukhādyanubhavaḥ) | tṛṣṇāvaipulyamupādānam | upādānanirjātaṃ punarbhavajanakaṃ karma bhavaḥ | bhavahetukaḥ skandhaprādurbhāvo jātiḥ | skandhaparipāko jarā (skandhajīrṇatetyarthaḥ) | skandhavināśo maraṇam | mriyamāṇasya mūḍhasya sābhiṣvaṅgasyāntardāhaḥ śokaḥ | śokenālapanaṃ paridevanam | cakṣurādipañcavijñānakāyasaṃyuktaṃ asātānuśayanaṃ duḥkhapaścāttāpaṃ duḥkha(m) | manasikāra saṃprayuktaṃ mānasaṃ duḥkha(m) daurmanasyam | ye cāpyanye evamādayaḥ kleśāḥ, upakleśā upāyāsāḥ (manovikalpajātamāyāśāṭhyadainyakāmarāgādayaste sarve | peyālam) ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)? That which, with respect to these very six elements, is the notion of unity, the notion of a compact mass, the notion of permanence, the notion of stability, the notion of eternity, the notion of pleasure, the notion of a being, a living being, a creature, a nourisher, a person, an individual, a human, a man; the notion of 'I-making' (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and 'mine-making' (<s>mamakāra</s>) — such and other manifold not-knowing: this is called ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). When ignorance is thus present, passion, aversion, and delusion (<s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, <s>moha</s>) arise with respect to objects. Therein, those [states of] passion, aversion, and delusion with respect to objects are called the karmic formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). The designation of a thing (the cognition, sensation, and volition of the [sense-]faculties) is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). The four appropriated aggregates (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>) that arise together with consciousness — that is name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>). The [sense-]faculties that are based upon name-and-form are the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>). The coming-together of the three factors is contact (<s>sparśa</s>) — meaning the coming-together of object, faculty, and consciousness. The experiencing of contact is sensation (<s>vedanā</s>). The fixating upon sensation is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) — fixation being the longing [for] and experiencing of pleasure and the like. The expansion of craving is appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>). The action (<s>karma</s>), born from appropriation, which generates renewed existence, is becoming (<s>bhava</s>). The manifestation of the aggregates caused by becoming is birth (<s>jāti</s>). The ripening of the aggregates is old age (<s>jarā</s>) — meaning the decay of the aggregates. The destruction of the aggregates is death (<s>maraṇa</s>). The inner burning of one who is dying, who is deluded and full of attachment, is sorrow (<s>śoka</s>). The lamenting that arises from sorrow is wailing (<s>paridevana</s>). The disagreeable sensation conjoined with the five sense-consciousnesses beginning with the eye, the painful aftermath, is bodily suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). The mental [suffering] conjoined with mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>) is dejection (<s>daurmanasya</s>). And whatever other defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) there are of this kind — these are the secondary defilements (<s>upakleśas</s>) and the tribulations (<s>upāyāsas</s>) — namely all the products of mental conceptualization: deceit, fraud, craftiness, wretchedness, sensual passion, and the like. (And so forth.)

body.text: punaraparam - tattve 'pratipattiḥ mithyāpratipattirajñānam (saṃvṛtiparamārthayorvibhāgājñānaṃ ajñānam) | avidyāyāṃ satyāṃ trividhāḥ saṃskārā abhinirvartante - puṇyopagā apuṇyopagā aniñjyopagāśceti saṃbhāvyante avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā iti | puṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ puṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati, apuṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ apuṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ (

children.translated_text: MŚālSū, Vaidya 112

children.text: ) bhavati, aniñjyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmaniñjyo pagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | idamucyate saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānamiti || tadevaṃ vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam || nāmarūpavivṛddhyā ṣaḍbhirāyatagadvāraiḥ kṛtyakriyā(ḥ) pravartante, tannāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamucyate || ṣaḍbhya āyatanebhyaḥ ṣaṭ sparśakāyasamūhāḥ pravartante, ayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśa ucyate || yajjātīyaḥ sparśo bhavati, tajjātīyā vedanā pravartate, iyaṃ sparśapratyayā vedanā ucyate || yastāṃ vedanā (vedayāti) viśeṣeṇāsvādayati abhinandati adhyavasa(sya?)ti (kāṅkṣati) adhitiṣṭhati, sā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇetyucyate || āsvādanābhinandanaṃ ādhyavasāyasthānam, na me priyarūpasātarūpaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇairviyogo bhavatu aparityāgaḥ, bhūyobhūyaśca prārthanā, idaṃ tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānamityucyate || evaṃ prārthayamānaḥ punarbhavajanakaṃ karma samutthāpayati kāyena manasā vācā, sa upādānapratyayo bhava ityucyate || yat karmanirjātānāṃ skandhānāmabhinirvṛttiḥ, sā bhavapratyayā jātirityucyate || yo jātyabhinirvṛttānāṃ skandhānāmupacayaparipākādvināśo bhavati, tadidaṃ jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamityucyate | (peyālam, tatra avidyādiṣu śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ peyālārthena nidarśitāḥ) ||
children.translated_text: ) of the karmic formations leading to the imperturbable, the consciousness becomes one leading to the imperturbable. This is called 'consciousness conditioned by the karmic formations' (<s>saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam</s>). Thus, name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) is conditioned by consciousness. Through the growth of name-and-form, the performance of functions proceeds through the six gateways of the sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>) — that is called 'the six sense-bases conditioned by name-and-form.' From the six sense-bases, the six groups of contact-bodies (<s>sparśakāyas</s>) arise — this is called 'contact conditioned by the six sense-bases.' Of whatever kind the contact is, of that same kind the sensation arises — this is called 'sensation conditioned by contact.' Whoever especially relishes that sensation that he feels, delights in it, fixates upon it, longs for it, and clings to it — that is called 'craving conditioned by sensation.' The relishing, the delighting, and the basis of fixation [in the thought:] 'May I not be separated from the five strands of sensual pleasure (<s>kāmaguṇas</s>) that are dear and agreeable, may there be no parting from them,' and the repeated yearning [for them] — this is called 'appropriation conditioned by craving.' Thus yearning, one arouses by body, mind, and speech the action (<s>karma</s>) that generates renewed existence — that is called 'becoming conditioned by appropriation.' The coming-into-being of the aggregates born from that action — that is called 'birth conditioned by becoming.' The destruction, through the accumulation and ripening, of the aggregates that have come into being through birth — that is called 'old age and death conditioned by birth.' (And so forth; therein, with respect to ignorance and the rest, sorrow, wailing, suffering, dejection, and tribulation are indicated by the sense of the abbreviation [<s>peyāla</s>].)

body.translated_text: Furthermore: the non-comprehension of reality, the erroneous comprehension, is not-knowing (<s>ajñāna</s>) — that is, the not-knowing which is the failure to distinguish between the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) and the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). When ignorance is present, three kinds of karmic formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) come forth: those leading to merit, those leading to demerit, and those leading to the imperturbable (<s>aniñjya</s>). [Thus] the karmic formations conditioned by ignorance are accounted for. Of the karmic formations leading to merit, the consciousness too becomes one leading to merit; of the karmic formations leading to demerit, the consciousness becomes one leading to demerit; (

body.text: tatra vijñānaṃ bījasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | karma kṣetrasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | avidyā tṛṣṇā ca kleśasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | karmakleśā vijñānabījaṃ janayanti | tatra karma vijñānabījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karoti, tṛṣṇā vijñānabījaṃ snehayati, avidyā vijñānabījamavakirati | satāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ vijñānabījasya abhinirvṛttirbhavati | tatra karmaṇo naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ vijñānabījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karomīti | tṛṣṇāyā api naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ vijñānabījaṃ snehayāmīti | avidyāyā api naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ vijñānabījamavakirāmīti | vijñānabījasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayai (pratītyotpādai)rjanita iti || api tu vijñānabījaṃ karmakṣetrapratiṣṭhitaṃ tṛṣṇāsnehābhisyanditamavidyāvakīrṇaṃ virohati | nāmarūpāṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati || sa cāsau nāmarūpāṅkuro na svayaṃkṛto na parakṛto nobhayakṛto neśvaranirmito na kālapariṇāmito na prakṛtisaṃbhūto nākāraṇādhīno nāpyahetusamutpannaḥ | atha ca mātāpitṛsaṃyogāt ṛtusamavāyādanyeṣāṃ ca pratyayānāṃ samavāyādāsvādātprabuddhaṃ (

children.translated_text: [Reference: MŚālSū, Vaidya 113]

children.text: ) vijñānabījaṃ tatratropapattyā mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati, asvāmikeṣu (dharmanairātmyena) adharmeṣu (pudgalanairātmyena) amameṣu aparigraheṣu apratyarthikeṣu ākāśasameṣu māyālambanasvabhāveṣu, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | (peyālam, peyālaśabdena sāvaśeṣaṃ nirdiśati) ||
children.translated_text: ) produces the sprout of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) in the mother's womb through rebirth here and there — in [phenomena that are] ownerless (through the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>), without a self (through the selflessness of persons), unappropriated, without opposition, equal to space, and having the nature of an illusory object — due to the completeness of causes and conditions. (The abbreviation [<s>peyāla</s>] indicates that [the exposition] continues with what remains.)

body.translated_text: Therein, consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is a cause by having the nature of a seed. <s>Karma</s> (action) is a cause by having the nature of a field. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) are causes by having the nature of defilements (<s>kleśas</s>). <s>Karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> generate the seed of consciousness. Therein, <s>karma</s> performs the field-function for the consciousness-seed; <s>tṛṣṇā</s> moistens the consciousness-seed; <s>avidyā</s> scatters [i.e., sows] the consciousness-seed. When these conditions are present, the production of the consciousness-seed occurs. Therein, <s>karma</s> does not think: 'I perform the field-function for the consciousness-seed.' <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> also does not think: 'I moisten the consciousness-seed.' <s>Avidyā</s> also does not think: 'I scatter the consciousness-seed.' The consciousness-seed also does not think: 'I am generated by these conditions (dependent arisings).' But the consciousness-seed, established in the field of <s>karma</s>, irrigated by the moisture of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, and sown by <s>avidyā</s>, germinates — and the production of the sprout of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) occurs. And this sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> is not self-made, not made by another, not made by both, not created by a god (<s>Īśvara</s>), not transformed by time, not arisen from primordial nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>), not dependent on a single cause, and yet not arisen without a cause. But through the union of mother and father, the conjunction of season, and the combination of other conditions, the consciousness-seed, awakened by relishing (

body.text: tadyathā - pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiścakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? cakṣuśca pratītya rūpaṃ ca ālokaṃ ca ākāśaṃ ca tajjamanasikāraṃ ca pratītya utpadyate cakṣurvijñānam | tatra cakṣurvijñānasya cakṣurāśrayakṛtyaṃ karoti, rūpamālambanakṛtyaṃ karoti, āloko 'vabhāsakṛtyaṃ karoti, ākāśamanāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karoti, tajjamanasikāraḥ samanvāharaṇakṛtyaṃ karoti | asatsu pratyayeṣu cakṣurvijñānaṃ notpadyate | yadā cakṣurādhyātmikamāyatanamavikalaṃ bhavati, evaṃ rūpālokākāśatajjamanasikārāścāvikalā bhavanti, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ samavāyāccakṣurvijñānasyotpattirbhavati | tatrāpi cakṣuṣo naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya āśrayakṛtyaṃ karomīti | rūpasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya avalambanakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ālokasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya avabhāsakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ākāśasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya anāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karomīti | tajjamanasikārasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya samanvāharaṇakṛtyaṃ karomīti | cakṣurvijñānasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayasamavāyairjanita iti | atha ca satsu pratyayeṣu cakṣurvijñānasyotpattiḥ prādurbhāvo bhavati | evaṃ śeṣāṇāmindriyāṇāṃ yathāyogaṃ kartavyam || tatra pratītyasamutpāde na kaściddharmo asmāllokātparalokaṃ saṃkrāmati, (iti śāśvatāntaniṣedhaḥ), asti ca karmaphalaprativijñaptihetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | (peyālam) | yathā agnirupādānavaikalyānna jvalati, upādānāvaikalyācca jvalati, evameva karmakleśajanitaṃ vijñānabījaṃ tatratatropapattyā āyatanapratisaṃdhau mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati, asvāmikeṣu adharmeṣu aparigraheṣu apratyarthikeṣu ākāśasameṣu māyālakṣaṇasvabhāveṣu, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | evaṃ ādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: For example: eye-consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) arises from five causes. Which five? Depending on the eye, form, light, space, and the corresponding mental attention (<s>tajjamanasikāra</s>), eye-consciousness arises. Therein, the eye performs the function of being the basis for eye-consciousness; form performs the function of being the object; light performs the function of illumination; space performs the function of non-obstruction; and the corresponding mental attention performs the function of directing. In the absence of conditions, eye-consciousness does not arise. When the internal sense-base (<s>āyatana</s>) of the eye is complete, and likewise form, light, space, and the corresponding mental attention are complete, then through the combination of all of them, eye-consciousness arises. And therein, the eye does not think: 'I perform the basis-function for eye-consciousness.' Form also does not think: 'I perform the object-function for eye-consciousness.' Light also does not think: 'I perform the illumination-function for eye-consciousness.' Space also does not think: 'I perform the non-obstruction-function for eye-consciousness.' The corresponding mental attention also does not think: 'I perform the directing-function for eye-consciousness.' Eye-consciousness also does not think: 'I am generated by this combination of conditions.' But when the conditions are present, the arising and manifestation of eye-consciousness occurs. The same should be applied accordingly for the remaining sense faculties. Therein, in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), no <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) whatsoever transmigrates from this world to the next world (this is the refutation of the eternalist extreme), yet there is the recognition of the results of <s>karma</s> due to the completeness of causes and conditions. (Abbreviation.) Just as fire does not burn when fuel is incomplete but burns when fuel is complete, even so the consciousness-seed generated by <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> produces the sprout of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) through rebirth here and there at the conjunction of the sense-bases (<s>āyatana-pratisaṃdhi</s>) in the mother's womb — in [phenomena that are] ownerless, without a self, unappropriated, without opposition, equal to space, and having the nature of an illusory mark — due to the completeness of causes and conditions. Thus should the foundation of conditions of internal dependent origination be understood.

children.translated_text: [MŚālSū, Vaidya 114]

children.text: ) tatra ādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairdraṣṭavyaḥ | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? yaduta na śāśvatataḥ, nocchedataḥ, na saṃkrāntitaḥ, parittahetutaḥ vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ, tatsadṛśānubandhataśceti | kathaṃ na śāśvatataḥ? yasmādanye maraṇāntikāḥ skandhāḥ, anye aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti | na tu ya eva maraṇāntikāḥ skandhāḥ, ta eva aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavantīti na | ato hetorna śāśvatataḥ || kathaṃ punarnocchedataḥ? na ca pūrvaniruddheṣu maraṇāntikeṣu skandheṣu aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti, nāpyaniruddheṣu | api tu maraṇāntikāḥ skandhā nirudhyante, tasminneva samaye aupapattikāśca skandhāḥ punarbhavanti, prādurbhavanti, tulādaṇḍonnāmāvanāmavat | ato nocchedataḥ || kathaṃ na saṃkrāntita iti? visadṛśāt sattvanikāyāt visabhāgāḥ skandhā jātyantareṣvabhinirvartante, ato na saṃkrāntitaḥ || kathaṃ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ? parīttaṃ karma kriyate, vipulaphalavipāko 'nubhūyate, ataḥ parittahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ || kathaṃ tatsadṛśānuprabandhataḥ? yathāvedanīyaṃ karma kriyate, tathāvedanīyo vipāko 'nubhūyate, atastatsadṛśānuprabandhataśceti ||
children.translated_text: ) Therein, the internal dependent origination should be viewed through five reasons. Which five? Not from the standpoint of eternalism, not from the standpoint of annihilationism, not from the standpoint of transmigration, from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause, and from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the [cause]. How is it not from the standpoint of eternalism? Because the aggregates at the time of death are different, and different aggregates at the time of rebirth arise. It is not that the very aggregates at death are the ones that arise at rebirth. Therefore, it is not from the standpoint of eternalism. How is it not from the standpoint of annihilationism? The aggregates at rebirth do not arise when the aggregates at death have previously ceased, nor when they have not yet ceased. Rather, the aggregates at death cease, and at that very moment the aggregates at rebirth come into existence and arise — like the rising and falling of the beam of a balance. Therefore, it is not from the standpoint of annihilationism. How is it not from the standpoint of transmigration? From a dissimilar class of beings, dissimilar aggregates arise in other births — therefore, it is not from the standpoint of transmigration. How is it from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause? A small <s>karma</s> is performed, yet a vast fruit of ripening is experienced — therefore, it is from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause. How is it from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the [cause]? Whatever type of <s>karma</s> is performed that is to be experienced [in a certain way], a corresponding type of ripening is experienced — therefore, it is from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the cause.

body.text: yaḥ kaścidbhadanta śāradvatīputra imaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ bhagavatā tathāgatena samyakpraṇītaṃ yathābhūtaṃ samyakprajñayā satatasamitaṃ ajīvaṃ nirjīvaṃ yathāvad (vi)parītaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akṛtaṃ asaṃskṛtaṃ apramitaṃ anāvaraḥaṃ śivaṃ abhayaṃ ahāryaṃ avyayaṃ avyupaśamasvabhāvaṃ paśyati, asatyato 'saktataḥ asārato rogato gaḥḍataḥ śalyato 'nityataḥ duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmataḥ samanupaśyati, sa na pūrvāntaṃ pratisarati - kimahamabhūvamatīte 'dhvani āhosvinnābhūvamatīte 'dhvani, ko nvahamabhūvamatīte 'dhvani | aparāntaṃ vā punarna pratisarati - kiṃ nu bhaviṣyāmyahamanāgate 'dhvani, āhosvinna bhaviṣyāmyahamanāgate 'dhvani, ko nvahaṃ bhaviṣyāmīti | pratyutpannaṃ vā punarna pratisarati - kiṃ nvidam, kathaṃsvididam, ki santaḥ ke bhaviṣyāma iti ||
body.translated_text: Whoever, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, sees this dependent origination — rightly propounded by the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, as it truly is — with right wisdom, constantly and continuously, as lifeless, without a living being, as it truly is, reversed, unborn, not really existent, unmade, unconditioned, immeasurable, unobstructed, auspicious, fearless, unassailable, imperishable, of the nature of non-cessation; who views it as unreal, unattached, essenceless, as a disease, as a boil, as a thorn, as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as without self — such a one does not resort to the past, [thinking:] 'Did I exist in the past, or did I not exist in the past? What was I in the past?' Nor does one resort to the future, [thinking:] 'Will I exist in the future, or will I not exist in the future? What will I be?' Nor does one resort to the present, [thinking:] 'What is this? How is this? Having been what, what shall we become?'

body.text: āryadaśabhūmake 'pyuktam - "tatrāvidyātṛṣṇokādānaṃ kleśavartmano vyavacchedaḥ, saṃskārā bhavaśca karmavartmano vyavacchedaḥ, pariśeṣaṃ duḥkhavartmano vyavacchedaḥ | (avidyāpratyayāḥ) saṃskārā ityeṣā pūrvāntikī apekṣā, vijñānaṃ yāvadvedaneti eṣā pratyutpannāpekṣā, tṛṣṇā yāvadbhava iti eṣā aparāntikī apekṣā, ata ūrdhvamasya pravṛttiriti | peyālam ||" "tasyaivaṃ (

children.translated_text: [MŚālSū, Vaidya 115]

children.text: ) bhavati - saṃyogāt saṃskṛtaṃ pravartate, visaṃyogānna pravartate | sāmagryā saṃskṛtaṃ pravartate, visāmagryā na pravartate | hanta, vayamevaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ viditvā asya saṃyogasya asyāśca sāmagryā vyavacchedaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, na cātyantopaśamaṃ sarva - saṃskārāṇāmadhigamiṣyāmaḥ sattvaparipācanatāyai" iti || idaṃ saṃkṣepānmohaśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: ) [reflection] arises: through conjunction, the conditioned operates; through disjunction, it does not operate. Through the aggregate of conditions, the conditioned operates; through the absence of the aggregate, it does not operate. Come, let us — having understood the conditioned as defiled by many faults — sever this conjunction and this aggregate of conditions, yet we shall not attain the utter cessation of all conditioned things, for the sake of maturing beings.' This, in brief, is the purification of delusion.

body.translated_text: In the noble <s>Daśabhūmaka</s> (Ten Stages [Sūtra]) too, it is said: 'Therein, ignorance, craving, and clinging constitute the severance of the path of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). Formations and becoming constitute the severance of the path of <s>karma</s>. The remainder constitutes the severance of the path of suffering. "Formations conditioned by ignorance" — this is the consideration regarding the past. "Consciousness up to feeling" — this is the consideration regarding the present. "Craving up to becoming" — this is the consideration regarding the future. From that point onward is its continuation.' ...abbreviated... 'For such a one, this (

body.text: tattvaṃ adharasaṃvṛttyakṣaraṃ saṃvṛtisvabhāvasarvadharmānutpādajñānam | tadāha - rūpaṃ tu dvividham, - varṇataḥ saṃsthānataḥ | te ca viṃśatidhā, tatra nīlādi nava, dīrghādyekādaśa | etatsarvaṃ rūpaṃ pāramārthikaṃ nāstīti pratijñā, svarūpeṇa hetuḥ | svahetunā tathaiva janito yathāvat paramārthikaṃ tu | yathā jalacandraḥ iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ | svarūpeṇa nāsti rupamityasyāyamabhiprāyaḥ | "pararūpeṇa rūpaṃ nāsti, svarūpeṇa vā ubhayarūpeṇa vā anubhayarūpeṇa veti" śāstram || utpādakahetupakṣo vikalpaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Reality (<s>tattva</s>) is the knowledge of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> whose nature is conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), the imperishable [truth] of lower convention. Thus it is said: form (<s>rūpa</s>) is twofold — in terms of color and in terms of shape. And these are of twenty types; among which, blue and so forth are nine, and long and so forth are eleven. The thesis is: all this form does not exist in ultimate reality (<s>pāramārthika</s>). The reason: by its own nature. Because it is produced by its own cause just as it is — but [this pertains only to] the ultimate. The example: like a reflection of the moon in water. The intended meaning of 'form does not exist by its own nature' is this: the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) [states]: 'Form does not exist by another's nature, or by its own nature, or by both natures, or by neither nature.' The position of the producing cause is [merely] conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>).

body.text: "na sat nāsat na sadasat na cāpyanubhayātmakam" | iti śāstram || ||
body.translated_text: 'Neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent, nor of the nature of neither' — thus the treatise [states].

body.text: kartṛpakṣo vikalpaḥ, tatra vilomnā nidarśanam |
body.translated_text: The position of the agent is conceptual construction. In that regard, the illustration is in reverse order:

children.translated_text: 'Neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent, nor of the nature of neither —
Reality freed from the four alternatives (<s>catuṣkoṭi</s>) — the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> know [this].'

children.text: "na svati nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ nāpyahetutaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Not from self, not from another, not from both, not without cause —

children.text: utpannā jātu dṛśyante bhāvāḥ kvacana kecana" ||
children.translated_text: are entities ever observed to arise anywhere whatsoever.'

body.text: tatra sato vidyamānasyotpādāyogāt vidyamānasyotpāde niravadhijanmaprasaṅgenānavasthā syāt | asadutpāde śaśaviṣāṇādīnāmutpādaprasaṅgāddhetoḥ prāk asaditi cet, tadeva cintyate - hetoḥ kimutpadyate sadasadvā? ubhayātmakasyotpāde viruddhadharmayorekasvabhāvatābhyupagamaḥ kathaṃ syāt? bhavatu viruddhadharmabandhanasvarūpaṃ ca pararūpanimittakam | tacca pararūpaṃ viruddhadharmābhyāsaḥ, sa ca bhedakaḥ | yatra parapratipattistatra kiṃ svarūpapratipattireva nāsti? pratītirasti, na svarūpapratipattiḥ | iyameva pratītiriti cet, tarhi apratītireva pratītiḥ | kiṃ brūmaḥ? atha ghaṭe paṭābhāvo 'sti | ghaṭaḥ paṭo na bhavatīti cet, miśrapratītirapi nāsti | tasmāt ghaṭo bhāvābhāvātmakaḥ, ataḥ siddhāḥ dvirūpatā | (

children.translated_text: [MŚālSū, Vaidya 116]

children.text: ) satyam, yadi vyavahartavyaikaśarīratāṃ tyaktvā prasahya rūpasyābhāvasya kiṃcidrūpaṃ syāt, tatra hyananyagatikobhayābhāvasvarūpopalambhāt abhāvo vyavahriyate ghaṭasyeti | tasmānna dvisvabhāvasya janma | ahetukotpannaṃ sarvaṃ sarvasmādutpadyate | atha hetuśabdo na nityaikaheturapekṣitaḥ, tasyotpāde sarvadaiva udayavyayau syātām, nityaikahetūtpannāpekṣāyā ayogāt | parāpekṣāyāṃ so 'pi anityaḥ, anityaṃ prati vikalpe sarvaṃ pūrvadāpadyate ||
children.translated_text: True — if, abandoning the single-bodied nature of what is to be conventionally dealt with, the absence of form were to have some form by force. For therein, since the own-nature of the non-existence of both is found with no other recourse, the non-existence of the pot is conventionally spoken of. Therefore there is no arising of what has a dual nature. [If things arose] without cause, everything would arise from everything. Now, if by 'cause' a permanent, single cause is not intended — upon its arising there would always be both arising and ceasing, because dependence on arising from a permanent single cause is impossible. When dependent on another, that [cause] too is impermanent. In the analysis of the impermanent, all the previous [difficulties] arise.

body.translated_text: Therein, because the arising of what [already] exists is logically impossible — if what already exists were to arise, there would be an infinite regress through limitless births. If the non-existent were to arise, there would be the absurd consequence that hare's horns and the like would arise. If [one says] 'it is non-existent before [arising] from the cause' — that itself is to be examined: does the existent, the non-existent, or [both] arise from the cause? In the arising of what has both natures, how could one accept that contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharma</s>) have a single nature? Granted that the nature which binds contradictory properties is caused by another's nature. And that other nature is the conjunction of contradictory properties, and that is a differentiator. Where there is cognition of the other, is there no cognition of own-nature at all? There is cognition, but not cognition of own-nature. If [you say] 'this very [thing] is cognition,' then non-cognition itself would be cognition. What are we to say? Now, in a pot there is the absence of cloth. If [one says] 'the pot is not cloth,' then there is no mixed cognition either. Therefore the pot has the nature of both existence and non-existence — hence the dual nature is established.

body.text: ataḥ svasmāt svayamutpadyate, anyasmādvā? nādyaḥ, prāganutpannaḥ svayamutpadyate | kimanutpannena rūpeṇa utpannena vā? anutpannena rūpeṇa anutpanna evotpannaḥ, anutpādena rūpeṇotpādāyogāt | atha prāgabhāvaḥ anutpannaśabdavācyaḥ, tat kiṃ prāgabhāvaḥ svena rūpeṇotpadyate? yadyevam, tadā abhāvanaṃ bhāvaḥ, paścādbhāva iti cet, tatra kimabhāva eva bhāvo bhavati? evaṃ sati abhāvasya punaḥpunarutpāde na prayojanamutpaśyāmaḥ, anavadhirutpādaśceti pararūpeṇotpāde ca apūrvakotpāda evāṅgīkṛtaḥ syāt | na caivaṃ siddhāntaḥ, utpannena utpāde vā saṃsāreṣu utpādaviramābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ prayojanābhāvaśca | dvitīyo 'pi na, anyasmādanyotpādāt | atha vā - svayameva anyarūpeṇa utpadyate, svātmani kāritravirodhaḥ, svātmani kriyāvirodhāt | na parata utpādaḥ, kutastatra siddhasya vā asiddhasya vā? uktamatrottaram - siddhasya utpādena kim, asiddhasya utpāda eva nāsti | ityādinā 'pi ubhayapakṣataḥ pratyekaṃ ye prasahu(jya?)nte, dvayorbhāve kathaṃ na bhavati iti nyāyāt || nāpyahetutaḥ, sarvatra sarvadotpādaprasaṅgāt, tathā anutpādaprasaṅgācca | kuta etat? asmātpramāṇāt | tadyathā - yat svatantraṃ na tat kādācitkam, yathā anyā sāmagrī | svātantryaṃ ca vivādapadam | tasmāt kādācitkatayā paratantratā vyāptā | yat kādācitkaṃ tatparatantram, yathā kuśūlatalanimīlitaṃ bījamaṅkurajananaṃ prati | kādācitkāśca bhāvāḥ | iti vivādapadam | yat paratantraṃ tatpratītyasamutpannam, yathā tadeva vījam | paratantrāśca bhāvā vivādapadam | yatpratītyotpannaṃ tannotpannaṃ svabhāvataḥ | yathā jalacandraḥ pratītyotpannaśca | paratantrāśca bhāvā vivādapadam || āryacandrapradīpasūtre -
body.translated_text: Therefore, does [a thing] arise from itself, by itself, or from another? Not the first: does [a thing] unarisen before [its arising] arise by itself? In what form — unarisen or arisen? If in its unarisen form, then it is just unarisen even when arisen, since arising is impossible in an unarisen form. Or, if prior non-existence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) is what is designated by the word 'unarisen,' then does that prior non-existence arise by its own nature? If so, then non-existence becomes existence. If one objects, 'It becomes existence afterward,' then: does non-existence itself become existence? In that case, we see no purpose in the repeated arising of non-existence, and the arising would be limitless. And in arising through another's form, one would have to accept causeless arising. Nor is this the established doctrine. For if [something already] arisen were to arise [again], there would be the unwanted consequence of no cessation of arising in the rounds of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and there would be no purpose [for arising]. The second alternative is also untenable, since what is other would arise from what is other [infinitely]. Or alternatively — if [a thing] arises by itself in another form, there is a contradiction of function with respect to itself, since action upon oneself is contradictory. Nor does arising occur from another. Why? Because for what is [already] established or for what is not established [among others]? The answer has already been given: for what is established, what is the need for arising? For what is not established, there is simply no arising. Thus, since the difficulties arise individually in both alternatives, by the principle 'how can they not arise when both are combined?' — [the third alternative is also untenable]. Nor [does anything arise] without a cause, because there would be the unwanted consequence of everything arising everywhere at all times, and likewise the unwanted consequence of nothing ever arising. How so? By means of this proof: Whatever is independent is not occasional, like [the absence of] an alternative causal complex. And independence is the point of dispute. Therefore, occasionality entails dependence. Whatever is occasional is dependent, like a seed concealed in a granary with respect to the production of a sprout. And all existents are occasional — this is the point of dispute. Whatever is dependent is <s>pratītyasamutpanna</s> (dependently arisen), like that very seed. And all existents are dependent — this is the point of dispute. Whatever is dependently arisen has not arisen from its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), like a reflection of the moon in water — and it is dependently arisen. And all existents are dependent — this is the point of dispute. In the <s>Āryacandrapradīpasūtra</s> —

children.translated_text: Whatever arises from conditions is indeed unborn;
its arising does not exist by its own nature.
Whatever depends on conditions is declared to be empty (<s>śūnya</s>);
whoever knows emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), that one is heedful.

body.text: iti vacanaṃ dhāryaṃ manasikāryaṃ sarvathā sarvadā sarvadarśibhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: This statement is to be held in mind and reflected upon in every way, at all times, by all who see [truly].

body.text: (madhyamaka - śālistambasūtraṃ samāptam ||)
body.translated_text: (The <s>Madhyamaka-Śālistambasūtra</s> is concluded.)
